trial_court: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Salem, H.M.O.P. No. 171 of 1986
outcome_detected: the order of the court below is set aside
facts_of_case: Wife married husband in 1977, gave birth to daughter, lived together till 1984, misunderstandings arose, wife left house, husband refused maintenance, wife filed M.C. No. 9 of 1985 for maintenance, trial court awarded Rs. 250 per mensem from 31.3.1986 onwards

legal_principles.principle: The right to claim maintenance is a statutory one.
legal_principles.held: Thus, the right of the wife to claim maintenance from the husband, even in those cases falling tinder Section 18(2) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, when she is obliged to live separately from her husband, is a statutory one.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act — Section 18

legal_principles.principle: The method and manner of enforcing the right to claim maintenance depend on the circumstances.
legal_principles.held: The method and manner of enforcing this right, would necessarily depend upon the circumstances obtaining in any particular case.

legal_principles.principle: The right to claim maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act is a special statutory right.
legal_principles.held: It is thus clear that the right to claim maintenance or litigation expenses under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, is not made available generally to the parties to a marriage, but only when a proceeding between the spouses is pending under that Act, and in that respect, the right conferred under Section 24 of that Act, is in the nature of a special statutory right not in any manner outside the provisions of Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: Order of the trial court below is set aside
